thread:
Maya S.: Heads-up: we keep seeing the same cache eviction incident popping up every 6-8 weeks. Can we formalize postmortem follow-ups so these don't recur?
Jordan (SRE): Definitely. My proposal: small issue template generated from the postmortem with explicit owner, fallback, and a 3-stage timeline (24h/7d/60d).
Priya Eng: Love the fallback idea. Too often owners get reassigned and tasks fall off. Fallback should be the oncall rotation.
Rafael PM: For comms cadence: ack within 30m, internal debrief within 12-24h, customer-facing note if user impact within 48-72h. Keep it consistent.
Maya S.: I'll sketch a lightweight YAML for the issue: severity, owner, fallback, immediate mitigation, short-term PR, long-term project link.
oncall-bot: New rule suggested: create postmortem-followup issue when PM labels a postmortem as "remediation-required".
Jordan (SRE): Also add a 90-day "recurrence check" reminder to the issue. If similar incidents exist, escalate to a pattern-owner review.
Priya Eng: We should auto-populate related incidents list in the issue to make pattern detection easier. Link to last 3 matching tags.
Rafael PM: Rotation policy: 2-week incident commander shifts, published calendar + handoff note template (open incidents, outstanding actions, blockers).
Maya S.: Action items: Maya draft YAML + example issue (Wed), Jordan wire automation (create issue & reminders), Priya add fallback logic, Rafael update calendar. 30-min sync next Mon to review.
Priya Eng: small ask: include a "qa_verify_by" field for short PRs so we don't assume they auto-ship.
Maya S.: Good call — adding qa_verify_by and est_risk. I'll post the draft in #eng-oncall when ready.
note: Thread represents a single Slack conversation string, messages in chronological order.
